_what: The name normalisation contract, read by BOTH languages. Never edit one side to make the other pass.
_why: A quote arrives from the odds provider, is normalised by normName() in
fantasy/worker/src/parse.mjs, and is stored as player_name_norm. The
crosswalk is built by fantasy-pipeline/norm.py and stored as search_name
and alias_norm. The join between every quote in this product and every
player it is about is a string equality between those two outputs.
So there are two implementations of one rule, in two languages, and there
is no way around that: the hot path is a Cloudflare Worker and the cold
path is Python because that is where nflreadpy lives. CLAUDE.md records
three extractors in this repo going silently wrong for less than this.
WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE WHEN THEY DRIFT is precisely what the database showed
the night this was written: 192 real quotes, real names, and every single
one unresolved. Nothing throws. Nothing is logged as an error. The product
just has no projections in it.
So neither implementation is the authority. This file is. fantasy/
check-worker.mjs drives normName against it and fantasy-pipeline/
test_norm.py drives norm() against it, and both run in CI.
_rules: drop a generational suffix (jr, sr, ii, iii, iv, v) as a whole word, with an optional trailing dot
delete everything that is not a-z or whitespace, which DELETES accented letters rather than transliterating them
collapse runs of whitespace to one space, and trim
_traps: ALTERNATION ORDER: 'ii' is listed before 'iii', so a naive engine could match the first two letters of III. Both engines backtrack to the word boundary and take 'iii'. Asserted.

ASCII WORD BOUNDARIES: JavaScript's \b treats an accented letter as a NON word character. Python's \b on a str is Unicode aware and treats it as a word character, so norm.py MUST compile with re.ASCII. Measured: without it, 'Nv' with a tilde gives 'v' in Python and '' in JavaScript. Asserted by the last two cases.

A NAME THAT IS NOTHING BUT A SUFFIX normalises to the empty string. Nothing may ever store that as an alias: it is a key that every empty normalisation matches. build_players.py refuses it and the guard asserts that too.
